canh-bon-thai-son-la.name: Thai-Style Buffalo Skin and Water-Taro Soup (Son La)
canh-bon-thai-son-la.serving_basis: One bowl per person, served hot with rice and the other dishes in a family meal.
canh-bon-thai-son-la.description: Canh bon is a familiar soup in the meals of some Thai communities in Son La. Bếp Việt's edited home recipe keeps the documented ingredients: prepared bon stems, tender buffalo skin, wild eggplant, mắc khén and herbs. The long simmer is stated clearly so cooks can plan ahead.
canh-bon-thai-son-la.finished_dish: A lightly thickened bowl with soft, nutty water-taro stems, tender chewy buffalo skin, wild eggplant and herbs; warm mắc khén aroma complements the naturally savory broth.
canh-bon-thai-son-la.serving: Ladle the hot soup into deep bowls, dividing the bon stems and buffalo skin evenly. Serve with hot rice and offer fresh chili separately so each person can adjust the heat.
tips: Buy bon stems intended for cooking from a trusted food seller. Wear gloves while peeling, rinse and soak in lightly salted water. Cook until completely tender; never taste uncooked or partly cooked bon.
Clean the buffalo skin and simmer it until tender before adding the bon. A pressure cooker can shorten this stage; follow the appliance instructions and check tenderness before continuing.
Add mắc khén and fresh herbs near the end to preserve their aroma. Season gradually because the buffalo skin and vegetables may vary in saltiness.
search_terms: water-taro stems and buffalo skin soup
canh-bon-thai-son-la.image_alt: A bowl of Thai-style Son La canh bon with tender water-taro stems, buffalo skin, wild eggplant and herbs in a lightly thickened broth; Bếp Việt image on a transparent background.
canh-bon-thai-son-la.time_note: About 6 hours, including preparation, a five-hour buffalo-skin simmer and cooking the bon stems and vegetables until tender.

ingredients.name: Water-taro stems (bon)
ingredients.notes: Use tender stems sold for cooking; peel the fibers, rinse and soak in lightly salted water.

ingredients.name: Cleaned buffalo skin
ingredients.notes: Have the hair removed by the seller; rinse well and cut into bite-size pieces.

ingredients.name: Wild bitter eggplant
ingredients.notes: Rinse and halve larger fruits; use a similar local wild eggplant if this variety is unavailable.

ingredients.name: Winter melon
ingredients.notes: Peel, remove mature seeds and cut into pieces; optional when out of season.

ingredients.name: Water
ingredients.notes: For simmering the buffalo skin and making the soup; add hot water if needed.

ingredients.name: Shallots
ingredients.notes: Peel and lightly crush.

ingredients.name: Lemongrass
ingredients.notes: Rinse, bruise and cut into sections.

ingredients.name: Toasted mắc khén pepper
ingredients.notes: Lightly toast and grind; add gradually.

ingredients.name: Lolot leaves
ingredients.notes: Rinse and slice into thin strips.

ingredients.name: Dill
ingredients.notes: Rinse and cut into short sections.

ingredients.name: Glutinous-rice flour
ingredients.notes: Mix with 30 ml cold water for a lightly thickened soup; optional.

ingredients.name: Fish sauce
ingredients.notes: Season after the buffalo skin and vegetables are tender.

ingredients.name: Salt
ingredients.notes: Add in small amounts and taste as you go.

ingredients.name: Fresh chili
ingredients.notes: Slice and serve separately to taste.

preparation_steps: Rinse the cleaned buffalo skin, drain and cut into bite-size pieces. Wearing gloves, peel the fibers from the bon stems, rinse several times, cut into sections and soak in lightly salted water for 15 minutes; drain.
Wash the wild eggplant and halve larger fruits; peel and cut the winter melon. Crush the shallots and lemongrass. Lightly toast and grind the mắc khén; rinse and slice the lolot leaves and dill.
cooking_steps: Put the buffalo skin, lemongrass and about 2 liters of water in a pot. Bring to a boil, skim the foam, lower the heat and simmer for about five hours or until tender; add boiling water to keep the skin submerged.
Add the peeled bon stems to the buffalo-skin broth and simmer gently for about 15?20 minutes, until tender. Add the bitter eggplant and winter melon, then cook until the vegetables are soft.
If desired, stir in the glutinous-rice slurry for a lightly thickened broth. Season with salt and fish sauce, add the mắc khén, lolot leaves and dill, simmer for 1–2 minutes, then turn off the heat.

ga-nau-mang-chua-hat-doi-hoa-binh.name: Hòa Bình Chicken Soup with Sour Bamboo Shoots and Hạt Dổi
aliases: Chicken and sour bamboo-shoot soup with hạt dổi
Hòa Bình chicken and sour bamboo shoots
ga-nau-mang-chua-hat-doi-hoa-binh.serving_basis: One bowl containing chicken and bamboo shoots per person, served hot with rice.
ga-nau-mang-chua-hat-doi-hoa-binh.description: Chicken soup with sour bamboo shoots and hạt dổi is associated with meals in Hòa Bình, where fermented bamboo shoots and toasted forest nutmeg bring a warm, tangy aroma. Bếp Việt's home version keeps the local flavor profile and simmers chicken and bamboo shoots gently until tender.
ga-nau-mang-chua-hat-doi-hoa-binh.finished_dish: A clear pale-golden broth with mild sourness, tender chicken pieces that hold their shape, lightly crisp bamboo shoots and the warm aroma of toasted hạt dổi.
ga-nau-mang-chua-hat-doi-hoa-binh.serving: Ladle equal portions of chicken, bamboo shoots and broth into bowls. Finish with scallions and cilantro and serve hot with steamed rice. Taste the broth before adding salt or fish sauce if the bamboo shoots are already salty.
tips: Taste the bamboo shoots before cooking. Briefly boil and drain them if they are too salty or sharply sour. Discard bamboo shoots with an unusual smell, slime or abnormal surface film.
Toast hạt dổi briefly in a dry pan until fragrant, then grind it. Avoid scorching it, which can make the soup bitter.
Cook until the meat beside the bone is fully done. If using a food thermometer, the thickest part of the chicken should reach at least 74°C (165°F).
search_terms: chicken soup with sour bamboo shoots and hạt dổi
Hòa Bình sour bamboo chicken soup
ga-nau-mang-chua-hat-doi-hoa-binh.image_alt: A bowl of Hòa Bình chicken soup with sour bamboo shoots and hạt dổi, showing tender golden chicken pieces, sliced giang bamboo shoots and herbs; Bếp Việt image on a transparent background.
ga-nau-mang-chua-hat-doi-hoa-binh.time_note: About 1 hour 20 minutes, including preparation, a short marinade and gently simmering the chicken with bamboo shoots until tender.

ingredients.name: Free-range chicken
ingredients.notes: Cut into even pieces; pat dry with a disposable paper towel.

ingredients.name: Sour pickled giang bamboo shoots
ingredients.notes: Cut into strips; briefly boil if excessively salty or sour.

ingredients.name: Shallots
ingredients.notes: Peel, crush and finely chop.

ingredients.name: Vegetable oil
ingredients.notes: For frying the shallots and searing the chicken.

ingredients.name: Water
ingredients.notes: Add hot water during simmering if needed.

ingredients.name: Hạt dổi (forest nutmeg)
ingredients.notes: Dry-toast until fragrant and grind; divide between the marinade and the finish.

ingredients.name: Fish sauce
ingredients.notes: Use for marinating and seasoning; adjust for the saltiness of the bamboo shoots.

ingredients.name: Salt
ingredients.notes: Season after the chicken and bamboo shoots have simmered together.

ingredients.name: Sugar
ingredients.notes: A small amount balances the sourness; optional.

ingredients.name: Scallions
ingredients.notes: Rinse and cut into sections.

ingredients.name: Cilantro
ingredients.notes: Rinse and chop for serving.

preparation_steps: Cut the chicken into even pieces and pat dry. Use a disposable paper towel, then wash hands and sanitize the knife and board. Marinate with half the fish sauce and a pinch of hạt dổi for 10 minutes.
Taste the sour bamboo shoots; rinse or briefly boil them if too salty, then drain. Toast and grind the hạt dổi, chop the shallots, and cut the scallions and cilantro.
cooking_steps: Heat the oil and fry the shallots until fragrant. Add the chicken and turn until the surfaces are sealed; add the bamboo shoots and stir-fry for another 3–4 minutes.

Pour in enough boiling water to cover the chicken and shoots. Bring to a boil, skim the foam, partially cover and simmer gently for about 30–35 minutes, until the chicken is tender and thoroughly cooked.
Season with the remaining fish sauce, salt and a little sugar if needed. Add the remaining hạt dổi near the end, turn off the heat and finish with scallions and cilantro.

cai-meo-xao-thit-ba-chi-moc-chau.name: Mộc Châu Mustard Greens Stir-Fried with Pork Belly
aliases: Moc Chau mustard greens stir-fried with pork belly
cai-meo-xao-thit-ba-chi-moc-chau.serving_basis: One small serving from a shared vegetable plate for four, alongside rice.
cai-meo-xao-thit-ba-chi-moc-chau.description: C?i m?o is a familiar local green on the M?c Ch?u plateau; local references note that it can be stir-fried with smoked meat. B?p Vi?t edits this into a home-style version with fresh pork belly, cooked in a quick stir-fry so the stems stay just tender, the leaves remain green and the pan does not become watery.
cai-meo-xao-thit-ba-chi-moc-chau.finished_dish: Deep-green leaves with crisp stems, browned pork-belly slices and fragrant garlic; lightly savory with a gentle sweet finish from the greens.
cai-meo-xao-thit-ba-chi-moc-chau.serving: Transfer the greens to a wide plate as soon as they are just cooked, sprinkle with ground pepper and serve hot with rice. Do not leave them in the pan, as residual heat will release water.
tips: Separate thick stems from leaves and add the stems first so they cook through without over-wilting the leaves.
Stir-fry a small batch over high heat. An overcrowded pan steams the greens and makes them watery.
Soy sauce and oyster sauce are already salty, so taste before adding salt. Cooked smoked pork can replace fresh belly, but reduce the salty seasonings.
cai-meo-xao-thit-ba-chi-moc-chau.image_alt: A plate of Mộc Châu mustard greens stir-fried with pork belly, with dark-green leaves, crisp stems and browned pork; Bếp Việt image on a transparent background.
cai-meo-xao-thit-ba-chi-moc-chau.time_note: About 42 minutes, including washing, slicing, a short marinade and a quick high-heat stir-fry.

ingredients.name: Cải mèo mustard greens
ingredients.notes: Separate the leaves, wash carefully, drain and cut the stems and leaves into separate sections.

ingredients.name: Pork belly
ingredients.notes: Slice into bite-size pieces.

ingredients.name: Lard or vegetable oil
ingredients.notes: Use just enough to fry the garlic and pork.

ingredients.name: Garlic
ingredients.notes: Peel, crush and mince.

ingredients.name: Light soy sauce
ingredients.notes: Main seasoning; choose a moderately salty variety.

ingredients.name: Oyster sauce
ingredients.notes: Adds mild savoriness; optional.

ingredients.name: Sugar
ingredients.notes: Balances the greens' gentle bitterness.

ingredients.name: Ground black pepper
ingredients.notes: Grind fresh and add at the end.

ingredients.name: Water
ingredients.notes: Add only if the pan dries before the stems soften.

preparation_steps: Wash each leaf of cải mèo, drain and cut the thick stems and leaves into separate 4–5 cm sections. Slice the pork belly thinly and mince the garlic.
Marinate the pork with half the soy sauce, the sugar and pepper for 10 minutes. Mix the remaining soy sauce and oyster sauce with one tablespoon of water for seasoning the greens.
cooking_steps: Heat a pan, add the lard or oil and fry the garlic until fragrant. Add the pork belly and stir-fry until cooked with lightly browned edges; transfer it temporarily to a plate.
Keep the pan hot, add the cải mèo stems and stir-fry for 1–2 minutes. Add the leaves and toss quickly until just wilted; add a little reserved water if the pan becomes dry.

Return the pork to the pan, pour in the soy and oyster sauce mixture, and stir-fry for 1–2 minutes until the greens are just tender while the stems remain crisp. Taste, add pepper and turn off the heat.

ga-nuong-mac-khen-tay-bac.name: Northwest Vietnamese Grilled Chicken with Mắc Khén
aliases: Thai-style grilled chicken with mắc khén
ga-nuong-mac-khen-tay-bac.serving_basis: One quarter of the grilled chicken per person, served with rice or vegetables.
ga-nuong-mac-khen-tay-bac.description: Grilled chicken with mắc khén is a well-known dish of the Thai people in Vietnam's Northwest. Bếp Việt's home version portions the chicken into large pieces for easier grilling while keeping the regional flavor profile. The chicken is grilled over steady medium coals, allowed to render its own fat and brushed with the mắc khén seasoning near the end to keep the spice aromatic rather than burnt.
ga-nuong-mac-khen-tay-bac.finished_dish: Golden-brown chicken with taut fragrant skin and juicy meat; mắc khén, ginger, lemongrass and a little chili create a warm aroma without overpowering the chicken.
ga-nuong-mac-khen-tay-bac.serving: Cut the chicken into pieces, arrange on a platter and serve hot with rice, fresh greens or boiled vegetables. Offer chẳm chéo separately so diners can adjust the saltiness.
tips: Grill over steady glowing coals rather than direct flames. Do not brush extra oil on the chicken; its own fat will render as it cooks.
Brush the mắc khén mixture on after the chicken surface has firmed. This helps release the aroma without scorching the spice.
Cook the chicken thoroughly. Use a thermometer to confirm the thickest section reaches at least 74°C (165°F). If using an oven, preheat it and rotate the tray midway for even cooking.
ga-nuong-mac-khen-tay-bac.image_alt: A platter of Northwest Vietnamese grilled chicken with golden-brown skin, lemongrass, ginger and mắc khén seasoning; Bếp Việt image on a transparent background.
ga-nuong-mac-khen-tay-bac.time_note: About 2 hours 15 minutes, including a one-hour marinade and grilling until fully cooked.

ingredients.name: Free-range chicken
ingredients.notes: Clean and quarter, or cut into large pieces for even grilling.

ingredients.name: Lemongrass
ingredients.notes: Rinse; bruise half for the marinade and mince the rest for the finishing paste.

ingredients.name: Ginger
ingredients.notes: Peel and crush.

ingredients.name: Toasted mắc khén pepper
ingredients.notes: Lightly toast and grind; divide between the marinade and finishing paste.

ingredients.name: Fresh chili
ingredients.notes: Remove seeds and mince; adjust to taste.

ingredients.name: Fish sauce
ingredients.notes: Use for the marinade and finishing paste.

ingredients.name: Salt
ingredients.notes: Season lightly, reducing it if the fish sauce is salty.

ingredients.name: Kaffir lime leaves
ingredients.notes: Rinse and slice thinly to finish the grilled chicken.

ingredients.name: Water
ingredients.notes: Mix with the finishing seasoning for easier brushing.

preparation_steps: Quarter the chicken or cut it into large pieces and pat dry. Mince the lemongrass, crush the ginger, and lightly toast and grind the mắc khén; divide the seasonings into marinade and finishing portions.

Mix part of the lemongrass, ginger, mắc khén, salt and half the fish sauce. Rub over the chicken, cover and marinate in the refrigerator for about one hour. Keep the finishing mixture separate from the raw chicken.
cooking_steps: Prepare a steady bed of glowing coals with no large flames. Put the chicken on a grill at a moderate distance, turning it evenly; allow the skin to firm and the chicken fat to render naturally without adding oil.

When the chicken is firm and nearly cooked, mix the remaining mắc khén, lemongrass, fish sauce and water. Brush a thin layer over the chicken and continue grilling, turning often to prevent the seasoning from burning.
Grill until the thickest part reaches 74°C (165°F), or the meat beside the bone is fully cooked. Rest for five minutes, cut into pieces, sprinkle with kaffir lime leaves and serve hot.

be-chao-moc-chau.name: Mộc Châu Quick-Fried Veal (Bê Chao)
aliases: Moc Chau young beef with ginger and lemongrass
be-chao-moc-chau.serving_basis: One shared platter for four, served hot with rice or fresh greens.
be-chao-moc-chau.description: Bê chao is a renowned specialty of the Mộc Châu plateau in Son La. Young veal is sliced, seasoned with ginger and lemongrass, then quickly fried in hot oil. Bếp Việt has edited the quantities for a home kitchen and divides the meat into small batches so the outside turns lightly golden while the inside stays tender.
be-chao-moc-chau.finished_dish: Golden pieces of veal with lightly crisp edges and a tender center, aromatic with ginger, lemongrass and kaffir lime leaves; served with a gently savory ginger-soy dip.
be-chao-moc-chau.serving: Drain the veal briefly on paper towels and serve immediately with crisp ginger, lemongrass and kaffir lime leaves. Serve the ginger-fermented-soy dip on the side with fresh greens to balance the richness.
tips: Cut the meat into pieces of even thickness and pat them dry before frying for even cooking and less oil splatter.
Fry in small batches in moderately hot oil; do not let the oil smoke. Thicker pieces need enough time for the center to cook through.
Fry the ginger, lemongrass and kaffir lime leaves separately for only a short time and remove them as soon as fragrant to avoid bitterness. Do not pour raw marinade over the cooked dish.
search_terms: fried veal with ginger and lemongrass
be-chao-moc-chau.image_alt: A platter of Mộc Châu bê chao with lightly crisp golden veal, ginger, lemongrass and kaffir lime leaves, served with ginger dip; Bếp Việt image on a transparent background.
be-chao-moc-chau.time_note: About one hour, including preparation, a 20-minute marinade, quick-frying in batches and mixing the dipping sauce.

ingredients.name: Veal
ingredients.notes: Choose tender shoulder or leg meat, cut into bite-size pieces and pat very dry.

ingredients.name: Lemongrass
ingredients.notes: Remove tough outer layers and slice thinly; divide between the marinade and garnish.

ingredients.name: Ginger
ingredients.notes: Peel and slice into thin strips; divide between the meat, dip and garnish.

ingredients.name: Garlic
ingredients.notes: Peel and mince for the marinade.

ingredients.name: Fish sauce
ingredients.notes: Season lightly; the dipping sauce is separately salty.

ingredients.name: Ground black pepper
ingredients.notes: Add to the marinade.

ingredients.name: Neutral frying oil
ingredients.notes: For quick-frying; some oil will remain after cooking.

ingredients.name: Tương bần fermented soybean sauce
ingredients.notes: Use for the dipping sauce and taste before adding sugar.

ingredients.name: Warm water
ingredients.notes: Thin the fermented soybean sauce to taste.

ingredients.name: Sugar
ingredients.notes: Balance the salty dip; optional.

ingredients.name: Kaffir lime leaves
ingredients.notes: Rinse, pat dry and slice into thin strips for a quick aromatic fry.

preparation_steps: Cut the veal into pieces about 1.5 cm thick and pat dry. Marinate with garlic, part of the ginger and lemongrass, fish sauce and pepper for 20 minutes; refrigerate if the kitchen is warm.
Stir the tương bần with warm water and some ginger, adding sugar if needed. Slice the remaining ginger, lemongrass and kaffir lime leaves separately for garnish.
cooking_steps: Heat oil in a deep saucepan until moderately hot but not smoking. Fry small portions of ginger, lemongrass and kaffir lime leaves for a few seconds, then lift them onto paper towels.

Divide the veal into two or three batches so the oil temperature stays steady. Fry each batch until golden-brown outside and fully cooked inside, turning as needed; avoid overcooking so the meat does not dry out.
Drain the veal briefly on paper towels, arrange on a platter and top with the crisp aromatics. Serve immediately with the ginger dip and fresh greens.
